A hash table is a data structure that implements an associative array abstract data type, a structure that can map keys to values. Internally, a hash table uses a hash function to compute an index into an array of buckets or slots, from which the desired value can be found. However, since different keys can hash to the same index (a situation known as a collision), hash tables often employ techniques to handle these collisions.
